note: Adapted from Roonwal & Chhotani 1997; the original is in English. The original work marks the alate as unknown (Imago: Unknown).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major soldier: head reddish brown, somewhat square, the sides nearly parallel, with a shallow median depression (head length to mandibular base 4.17, maximum width 3.53 mm); with a Y-shaped suture; bearing numerous hairs of medium length. Anteclypeus trapezoidal; postclypeus not distinctly differentiated; labrum wider than long, hairy throughout, the hairs at the anterior end longer. Antennae 23-segmented. Compound eyes and ocelli small. Mandibles robust (length 2.71 mm), with well-developed marginal teeth. Postmentum long (length 2.91, maximum width 1.02, minimum width 0.87 mm), flat, the sides nearly parallel. Anterior part of the pronotum slightly raised and convex, the posterior margin deeply concave in the middle. Tarsi 4-segmented. Minor soldier: generally as in the major soldier but smaller (head length to mandibular base 3.20, maximum head width 2.91 mm); antennae 25-segmented; sides of the postmentum wavy; posterior margin of the pronotum with only a weak notch.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Not described by Akhtar, who only figures the mandibles: the mandibles bear 2 marginal teeth (the two teeth of the left mandible farther apart, those of the right mandible close together).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Distribution: Pakistan, known only from the type locality, Chaman, Baluchistan. Habits: damaging logs and constructing longitudinal galleries in wood. Nomenclatural note: Chaudhry and Ahmad first used the name in 1972 without a description (nomen nudum); in 1974 Akhtar formally described the soldier and worker, in Biologia (Lahore) 20: 17–40; the soldier holotype is deposited in the Department of Zoology, University of the Punjab, Lahore. The original notes that the alate is unknown.
